claimsToVerify: One denarius was a typical daily wage for unskilled laborers in the early-to-mid Roman imperial period (subject to inflation in later periods).
Bread and cheap local wine were relatively inexpensive staples for Roman city dwellers compared to rent.
Roman insulae (tenement blocks) were notoriously crowded, expensive, and vulnerable to catastrophic fires.
